summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted from rehabilitation for altered mental status and hypoxia. She presented with somnolence and respiratory distress, requiring temporary high-flow oxygen. Her condition was attributed to acute on chronic respiratory and heart failure, exacerbated by noncompliance with CPAP. A chest X-ray confirmed pulmonary edema, and she was treated with IV diuretics, with transition to daily torsemide. She developed recurrent right leg cellulitis, prompting a 7-day course of clindamycin and wound care with compression. Despite a documented cefepime allergy, she received a dose in error but did not develop a rash. Urine culture showed Proteus mirabilis colonization, but asymptomatic status precluded treatment. She improved neurologically and respiratory with oxygen weaning, was deemed stable, and discharged to extended care with follow-up arranged for cardiology, pulmonology, and dermatology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
